author: Ifmyante
text:
Hi all

I've been doing lots of deliberating lately about my place in the world of trading.

When I first saw a chart, I thought "Yes!! I'll solve that puzzle and make a fortune from it!!!"

I should've known at the time that all I really wanted to do was simply solve the puzzle.

As you have probably guessed already, I love to teach what I have
learned. Many of you have also found that I've given out all the
information necessary to work out the entire market. Sure, you had to
put in a lot of work to make the lessons your own, but all the signposts
 and pitstops were there to help you on your journey.

If I teach any more, I think I'd be taking everyone straight to the finish line.

The problem for me is, I still want to teach it.

I've been looking at the other analysis schools and awarding bodies, and
 none of them come even close to reading the market fully. The teachings
 of RTM blow them all out of the water.

I believe that an RTM Degree should be THE most prestigious qualification in trading.

So I'm considering running an online trading university, with a complete
 syllabus, teaching everything that needs to be learned - a complete
course in analysis, and also a complete course in trading methods, with
 dedicated teachers helping the students all the way to the final exams
and graduation.

Some say that those who can, do, and those who can't, teach. Well, we've
 made enough great traders that I certainly have no need to trade for
myself, so perhaps I should just keep doing what I love to do - teach

Let me know what you guys think about this

Best

If

author: Springger
text:
Great idea IF. In that case, put me down as student number 0. The one
at the top of the line, yea the one in front of the first. .

Its a great idea. Some students need more help than others, the forums
can only provide so much help. The rest of the time you need a mentor to
 help you, guide you, coach you along the way All professional careers
have a professional program, as well as a period of internship (
interpreted as coaching). Trading should be the same. Its amazing how
some guys can eke out a fortune with material they discovered on various
 forums. Those are the lucky few. Imagine flying with a pilot who
trained on forums or Flight Simulator X. Its also comparable to visiting
 a doctor who trained of YouTube.

The rest of us? Not so lucky. That's where a complete program comes in
handy. Of course, no one ever said it was going to be easy. Having a
mentor sure might even make the journey faster. I've been on mine since
2009.................

IMO, give it a shot.

author: Jambowlyai
text:
That certainly is an interesting proposition If. Let me tell you how
things look from my end. I'm sure my view will be similar to others
though I have no idea what percentage.

I would have no problem paying money to be able to see the market as you

I guess what I mean is that I want to get to the finish line, I have

So at this point I would certainly be interested in a thorough,

author: Ifmyante
text:
AERO wrote: its maybe time to move on, onto other different areas.

I think you know my personality quite well Miky

I've tried many many many disciplines in my life, and as soon as I had
one mastered, I lost interest and moved on to learn the next.

To be honest, I'm running out of new things to try.

Yes, although the movement of price will forever keep me enthralled,
trading them is beginning to interest me less and less. But there are
still many challenges for me yet to try in the trading business.

We're not far off being compliant, so there'll be lots to do setting up
the fund - setting up the software, getting investors, and keeping the
traders in top condition.

But for now I'm itching to get this course finished and teachers taught.
 Believe me, that'll give me no time to dream of new horizons!

Sure, once all is established, and successors prove themselves to do my
jobs better than I, I'll be delighted to leave them to it, so I can move
 on to my next projects - I'm still convinced that RTM will be the
foundation for them though - See the fourth paragraph of the
 Objectives
 page

cracking the code. Reading PA should not be subjective. If it is a skill

 address this basic frustration. Trading is a confidence game - if you
don't have it with your methodology you end just staying on the
"learning treadmill" - which as fascinating as it is, starts getting a
bit old. I wish you the best with whatever choices you make. FX
